guardrail: Research is hypothesis generation only. No item in this file is allowed to change live predictions until separately validated.
research_summary: Evidence supports conditioning momentum versus reversal on intraday timing, liquidity, turnover, news intensity, and price-volume path. Continuation is more plausible when returns reflect information and liquidity is sufficient; exhaustion and reversal are more plausible after transient liquidity pressure, widening spreads, volume climax, failed reclaim, or weak late bounces. Sequence discovery should use strictly chronological discovery and validation splits. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4069509&utm_source=openai))

hypotheses.title: Bounce-size decay predicts exhaustion
hypotheses.claim: For comparable catalyst-driven advances, the second and third bounce from a pullback low have lower median rebound size and higher failure probability than the first bounce, especially when each bounce makes a lower high.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Repeated tests may consume nearby demand while failed highs reveal declining buying pressure.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 5-minute and 30-minute return, probability of a 5% or 10% decline, and minutes until failure after bounce confirmation.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher bounce number, smaller bounce size, lower high, and declining volume should predict weaker continuation and faster downside.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Event study with stock-day clustered errors; define bounces ex ante using volatility-scaled pivots and evaluate untouched future bars with purged walk-forward splits.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Monotonic deterioration across bounce numbers, statistically reliable calibration, and improvement over price-only and volume-only baselines in at least two unseen periods.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No monotonic pattern, instability across liquidity buckets, or disappearance after spread and catalyst controls.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Volume climax followed by contraction distinguishes exhaustion from continuation
hypotheses.claim: After a large impulse, an extreme volume spike followed by falling volume, narrowing range, and inability to hold above VWAP predicts exhaustion more often than a continuation characterized by renewed volume expansion and sustained VWAP acceptance.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Volume shocks may represent information arrival, but subsequent intraday behavior can separate absorption from persistent demand.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of a new high within 30 minutes and probability of a 5% falloff within 60 minutes.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Climax plus contraction and VWAP loss should predict failure; contraction followed by expansion above VWAP should predict continuation.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Construct impulse events without future information; compare matched event-study cohorts and use nested walk-forward threshold selection.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: At least 20% relative improvement in out-of-sample AUC or calibration over impulse-return and VWAP baselines, with economically meaningful net-of-spread separation.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No incremental value after controlling for realized volatility, catalyst, and liquidity, or strong dependence on one ticker or event type.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Liquidity determines whether a reclaim is real
hypotheses.claim: A failed reclaim of a prior high or VWAP is more predictive of rapid downside when quoted spreads widen, depth or turnover deteriorates, and price impact rises; tight spreads and renewed turnover increase the chance of a true reclaim.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Microstructure evidence links short-horizon reversal to temporary liquidity imbalances, while illiquid low-priced stocks face larger price impact and wider spreads. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/SSRN_ID1616184_code31361.pdf?abstractid=1509466&mirid=1&utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of holding above the reclaimed level for 5 minutes and probability of a 5% decline within 60 minutes.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Wider spreads, lower depth, and weaker turnover should increase failed-reclaim severity and shorten time-to-failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Use quote-and-trade event studies with realistic execution bands; stratify by price and float and validate on later ticker-months.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Stable incremental predictive power after controlling for return, volatility, and news, plus positive performance under conservative spread and slippage assumptions.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Effect vanishes after excluding stale quotes, odd lots, halts, or low-observation symbols.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Late-session strength has conditional continuation value
hypotheses.claim: A strong move that persists into the final 30 minutes is more likely to continue into the next session when it is accompanied by high liquidity, small overnight gap risk, and broad intraday acceptance; isolated late spikes with weak depth are more likely to reverse.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: The final half-hour has documented cross-sectional momentum and unusually high auction activity, but closing-hour signals may mix information with liquidity demand. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/4934543.pdf?abstractid=4934543&mirid=1&utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Next-session opening-to-30-minute return, probability of a new intraday high, and overnight-to-open reversal.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Persistent, liquid late strength should predict continuation; illiquid vertical late strength should predict reversal or gap failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Chronological ticker-day panel with separate close-to-open and open-to-30-minute outcomes; include auction-aware and no-auction robustness tests.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Effect remains after transaction-cost adjustment and survives separate validation by market regime, price bucket, and catalyst class.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Only raw returns predict outcomes, or the signal is entirely explained by overnight gaps and auction mechanics.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Step-plateau-reacceleration is a distinct multi-session state
hypotheses.claim: A multi-session pattern of positive step, higher-level plateau with reduced volatility and maintained volume, followed by renewed expansion has higher subsequent continuation probability than a single-session spike of equal cumulative return.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Price acceptance at a higher level may indicate information diffusion and reduced immediate supply before a second repricing.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Next-session and next-five-session excess return, probability of a fresh high, and maximum adverse excursion.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Tighter higher-level plateaus with stable liquidity and later volume expansion should predict stronger continuation than vertical one-day moves.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Define states using only completed sessions; use rolling hidden-state or change-point estimation and validate on later calendar blocks and ticker cohorts.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: State-conditioned outcomes remain significant across at least three chronological test windows and outperform cumulative-return, volatility, and catalyst baselines.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Pattern depends on arbitrary thresholds, fails under threshold perturbations, or loses value after controlling for catalyst persistence and market trend.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Unsupervised motif discovery can find unnamed continuation and failure states
hypotheses.claim: Chronologically discovered multivariate motifs in normalized price-volume-microstructure sequences will identify recurring states with materially different forward outcomes, including quick bounces versus true new-high continuations.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Named setups may omit recurring shapes; motif, shapelet, clustering, and change-point methods can search for unknown structures while preserving test-set integrity. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.01819?utm_source=openai))
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward 5-minute, 30-minute, and next-session returns; new-high probability; 5% and 10% falloff probability; time-to-failure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Some discovered motifs should show stable positive continuation and others stable failure, but direction must be learned rather than assumed.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Use an early discovery window for motif extraction and clustering, freeze motif definitions, then test only on later unseen dates; repeat with rolling discovery-to-test windows and nested hyperparameter selection.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: At least one motif has stable forward separation across multiple unseen periods, meaningful sample size, robustness to normalization choices, and improvement over supervised baselines without leakage.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Motif labels drift materially, forward separation disappears after costs or regime controls, or performance relies on re-fitting using the validation/test period.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

important_caveats: Do not treat statistical continuation as a trade recommendation; evaluate execution, borrow, halts, slippage, and data availability separately.

Low-priced and microcap securities can have wide spreads, sparse depth, fragmented quoting, and manipulation risk, making bar-based backtests optimistic. ([investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/investor-2?utm_source=openai))
Use split-adjusted and corporate-action-corrected data, timestamp news at first availability, and exclude future-known labels from feature construction.
Overlapping events, ticker changes, delistings, halts, and survivorship bias require explicit handling.
Thresholds should be volatility- and tick-size-aware rather than fixed percentage rules across all stocks.
A 5% or 10% falloff may be mechanically impossible or economically irrelevant for some price, spread, or halt conditions.
research_gaps: Reliable intraday datasets linking consolidated trades, quotes, depth, halts, news timestamps, float changes, and borrow availability.
Causal separation of genuine catalyst information from promotional or manipulative attention shocks.
Formal estimation of bounce number when pivots overlap or occur during halts.
Whether order-book imbalance and queue dynamics improve prediction beyond spread, turnover, and VWAP features.
How motif stability changes across decimalization, tick-size, venue, and market-structure regimes.
Whether multi-session states transfer across sectors, exchanges, price levels, and catalyst categories.
